disagreement: 2025 market reported as US$795.6bn (WSTS, June 2026), US$791.7bn (SIA, Feb 2026, WSTS data) and US$793bn (Gartner preliminary, Jan 2026); growth 26.2%, 25.6% and 21% respectively.
possible_reasons: data vintage: SIA figure published before WSTS revisions
methodology: Gartner builds from vendor revenue; WSTS from member-reported sales
different 2024 base (WSTS 630.5 vs Gartner 655.9) drives the growth-rate gap
preliminary vs final
rationale: Most recent revision of the reference industry statistic; SIA's figure is an earlier vintage of the same data.
remaining_uncertainty: Levels agree within ~0.5%; growth rates differ by 5 points because the two publishers' 2024 bases differ by ~US$25bn. Gartner's final 2025 figure not yet seen.

disagreement: 2024 market: WSTS US$630.5bn vs Gartner final US$655.9bn vs Gartner preliminary US$626bn.
possible_reasons: different populations (Gartner vendor revenue may include items WSTS excludes, e.g. non-member or captive devices)
Gartner prelim-to-final revision of ~US$30bn
methodology undisclosed in public releases
rationale: Publishers measure differently defined populations and do not publish reconciliations; neither is 'wrong'.
remaining_uncertainty: Cause of the ~4% gap between WSTS and Gartner final, and of Gartner's large revision, unknown.

disagreement: WSTS forecast 2026 at US$975.5bn in Dec 2025 but US$1.51tn in June 2026.

rationale: Later vintage incorporates actual H1 2026 data (e.g. July 2026 monthly sales +135% YoY).
remaining_uncertainty: 2026 remains a forecast; volatility of memory prices makes it highly uncertain.

disagreement: Foundry industry quoted as ~US$250bn (2023, TSMC Foundry 2.0) vs US$115bn (2023, old definition) vs ~US$46.3bn per quarter top-10 foundry services (4Q25, TrendForce).

different periods (annual 2023 vs quarter 4Q25)
rationale: Definitional difference, not a factual conflict.

disagreement: Official registration data give phase-1 registered capital of CNY 138.7bn (2014); a USITC staff paper describes $150bn 'from the central and provincial governments'.
possible_reasons: different populations: national fund alone vs national plus provincial/municipal funds
target vs raised/registered capital
currency (CNY vs USD) and period (2014 registration vs 2017 status)
rationale: The figures measure different things; the USITC paper itself states the national fund had roughly $21bn (consistent with CNY 138.7bn) and that $150bn was a combined target.

disagreement: SIA reported $627.6bn for 2024 in February 2025 and $630.5bn for 2024 in February 2026.

rationale: Later revised figure from the same data series (WSTS via SIA) supersedes the preliminary figure.

possible_reasons: Different populations: WSTS aggregates member-reported sales; Gartner estimates vendor revenue across all vendors
Gartner figure is preliminary (Jan 2024), WSTS figure is full-year (Feb 2024)
Different treatment of foundry/captive revenue and category definitions
rationale: Both are credible but measure different populations; use one series consistently. WSTS is the official industry statistic used by SIA.
remaining_uncertainty: Exact definitional differences between WSTS and Gartner not documented in sources read.
topic: Size of the 2023 semiconductor market decline

disagreement: SIA/WSTS figures imply memory sales fell ~29% in 2023 (US$130bn to US$92.3bn); Gartner estimated a 37% decline.

SIA 2022 memory figure is rounded
Gartner preliminary vs WSTS final
rationale: Both show memory fell far more than the overall market; exact magnitude depends on data series.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether the gap is purely definitional; WSTS official memory growth rate for 2023 not read directly.

disagreement: NIST's CHIPS fact sheet says the investment tax credit is up to 25% of qualified capital expenditures; the current statute and IRS guidance give 35% for facilities placed in service after 2025.
possible_reasons: different period: the NIST fact sheet predates P.L. 119-21 (2025), which raised the rate
NIST text says 'expected to be up to 25%' — a pre-amendment description
rationale: The statute (26 USC 48D) and IRS guidance citing P.L. 119-21 section 70308 are the controlling, more recent tier-1 sources; 25% still applies to facilities placed in service before 2026.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether the credit's 31 Dec 2026 construction-start deadline will be extended (proposals exist but were not verified).
topic: US section 48D investment tax credit rate

disagreement: BCG/SIA give an average wafer fabrication cycle time of about 12 weeks; ASML says the process can take up to four months from design to mass production.
possible_reasons: different definitions: fab cycle time for one wafer lot vs elapsed time from design release to mass production
average vs upper bound
ASML figure's scope (whether it includes mask making, back-end, ramp) not defined
rationale: The figures measure different intervals; neither contradicts the other. A newcomer should read 12 weeks as front-end only, excluding mask making and back-end.
remaining_uncertainty: No tier-1 source found that breaks down total lead time (tape-out -> masks -> fab -> sort -> assembly/test -> shipment) by stage for current nodes.
topic: How long it takes to make a chip

remaining_uncertainty: No primary production statistics for semiconductor-grade neon by country were found; the true share of chip-grade supply may differ from both.
